# Refusal Parity: is safety repair language-fair?

[![CI](https://github.com/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity/actions/workflows/ci.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity/actions/workflows/ci.yml)
[![Code: Apache-2.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/code-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
[![Data: CC BY-NC 4.0](https://img.shields.io/badge/data-CC%20BY--NC%204.0-lightgrey.svg)](LICENSE-DATA)
[![Python 3.12](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.12-blue.svg)](pyproject.toml)
[![Data on Hugging Face](https://img.shields.io/badge/%F0%9F%A4%97%20data-refusal--parity-yellow.svg)](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity)

**Abdullah Ibn Mahdi Abtahi** · Ingramin ·
paper: [`paper/main.pdf`](paper/main.pdf) · v{{version}}

This repository audits whether *refusal repair* (activation steering gated per prompt, and weight-space repair) treats
languages fairly. The study model is Cohere's Tiny Aya (3.35B). It covers ten [MultiJail](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DAMO-NLP-SG/MultiJail)
languages in three resource tiers and has a pre-registered analysis plan. The pipeline is built on the Lexsi
open-source stack: **CuratorKIT → CircuitKIT → SafeTune → AuditKIT**.

> ⚠️ **Content warning.** The evaluation uses harmful requests from public red-teaming benchmarks, and some model
> responses are harmful. Responses and steering artifacts are distributed only through gated Hugging Face repos.

## Main findings (Tiny Aya Earth, A100, Qwen3Guard-4B; v{{version}})

![Teaser figure: (a) mean safe-response rate against worst-language benign refusal across repair arms on Tiny Aya Earth, with arrows from the unrepaired model (E0) to pooled split-conformal threshold (CPOOL-S) and per-language split-conformal thresholds (EORS-S); (b) mean benign refusal without and with the English greeting prefix across E0, CPOOL-S, and EORS-S.](docs/assets/fig1_teaser.png)

Values are generated from the result files by the same macros as the paper: the threshold-rule rows from `runs/controls_report.json` and `runs/arms_report.json` (read by the dated pre-registration rules), the detector row from `runs/B0/h1.json`, the comparator row from `runs/GEM-lite/judged.jsonl`. 95% paired bootstrap intervals over prompt ids.

| Finding | Estimate |
|---|---|
| At a matched false-refusal budget (ε = .05), per-language split-conformal thresholds vs one pooled threshold: worst-language benign refusal | **{{CtlFivePoolWorstBrr}} → {{CtlFiveEorsWorstBrr}}**, {{CtlFiveMaxBrr}} pp [{{CtlFiveMaxBrrLo}}, {{CtlFiveMaxBrrHi}}]; mean {{CtlFiveMeanBrr}} pp [{{CtlFiveMeanBrrLo}}, {{CtlFiveMeanBrrHi}}] |
| …and the price: harmful-prompt refusal in the low-resource tier ({{lrl_langs}}) | {{CtlFiveLrlHrr}} pp [{{CtlFiveLrlHrrLo}}, {{CtlFiveLrlHrrHi}}]; {{CtlFiveHrrLossLang}} {{CtlFiveHrrLossPts}}, {{CtlFiveHrrGainLang}} {{CtlFiveHrrGainPts}} |
| Per-language false-firing bound on held-out prompts: languages above the predictive band | {{CtlFiveValidAbove}} of {{n_langs}} at ε = .05, {{CtlTenValidAbove}} of {{n_langs}} at ε = .10 |
| Gate separates XSTest's unsafe from safe contrast prompts (harm, not only dataset style) | AUROC {{CtlStyleAuc}} (every language ≥ {{CtlStyleAucMin}}) |
| A benign "Good morning." prefix (ε = .10), mean benign refusal of the repaired model | {{CtlGreetBrrEors}} → {{CtlGreetBrrEorsGreet}} (`EORS-S`), {{CtlGreetBrrPool}} → {{CtlGreetBrrPoolGreet}} (`CPOOL-S`); unrepaired {{GreetBrrEZero}} → {{GreetBrrEZeroGreet}} |
| SafeTune's English keyword refusal detectors: highest recall outside English | {{HOneRecallOtherMax}} |
| Closed comparator (Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite) safe-response rate: same-family judge vs Qwen3Guard (post hoc) | {{GemGSrr}} vs {{GemQSrr}} |

Equal false-refusal rates across languages whose gate-score distributions differ force unequal protection. Which error to equalise is a deployment decision; the paper reports both at matched budgets.

## How the study is organised

The code is one package, `src/refusal_parity/`, with a subpackage per pipeline stage. Every module opens with a
docstring stating its purpose, the paper section it serves and its outputs. Run modules from `src/` as
`python -m refusal_parity.<stage>.<module>`; the `Makefile` wraps the common entry points.

![Study pipeline diagram showing the seven subpackages in src/refusal_parity/ connected to the Lexsi open-source stack (CuratorKIT, CircuitKIT, SafeTune, AuditKIT).](docs/assets/pipeline.png)

| Stage | What happens | Subpackage (main modules) | Output |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1. Data | MultiJail (harmful) + XSTest-safe translated with NLLB (benign), QA by GlotLID and back-translation chrF; CuratorKIT clean / dedup / provenance; ids kept only if parallel in all 10 languages | `data/` (`translate_xstest`, `build_data`, `build_pgp_val`) | `data/eval.jsonl` |
| 2. Activations | Last-token residual stream at every layer (decoder only, hooks) | `activations/` (`mech`, `gate_acts`) | `runs/mech_*`, `runs/gate_acts_*` |
| 3. Steering | Steering vectors, condition directions and gate thresholds fitted offline from calibration activations; built on SafeTune's `CASTModel`; ReSta weight streaming | `steering/` (`arms`, `steer`, `lazy_sd`, `choose_alpha`) | `arm_config.json` per run |
| 4. Generation | AuditKIT `generate` with each arm (A100 via `scripts/colab_gen.sh`) | `generation/` (`run_arm`, `generate`) | `runs/<arm>/responses.jsonl` |
| 5. Scoring | AuditKIT `evaluate`: Qwen3Guard-4B (primary), SafeTune keyword detectors, GlotLID fidelity, Gemini (secondary); judges validated against human labels | `scoring/` (`audit`, `judge`, `gemini`, `validate_judges`) | `runs/<arm>/judged.jsonl` |
| 6. Analysis | Paired McNemar (Holm) and paired bootstrap over prompt ids; pre-registered reports, hypotheses H1/H3, gate diagnostics | `analysis/` (`analyze`, `arms_report`, `controls_report`, `h1`, `h3`, `gate_proxy`, `failure_gate`, `spoof`) | `runs/arms_report.json`, `runs/controls_report.json` |
| 7. Paper | Every number is a generated LaTeX macro with its source; figures carry provenance JSON | `reporting/` (`paper_numbers/`, one module per paper part; `figures_results`, `figures_diagnostics`, `cohere_style`) | `paper/` |
| Circuits | CircuitKIT discovery on a remote GPU and cross-language comparison (a negative result, appendix D) | `circuits/` (`circuit_spec`, `colab_circuit`, `compare`) | `runs/circuitkit/` |

Shared: `common.py` (paths, languages, seeds, pinned revisions, constrained GlotLID) and `track.py` (MLflow).

## Reproduce

```bash
make setup          # Python 3.12 venv with the exact versions in pyproject.toml (uv)
make data           # released data from Hugging Face -> data/, runs/ (GATED=1 adds responses and activations)
make test           # unit tests, CPU, under a minute
make report         # pre-registered comparisons (the gate-level part needs GATED=1)
make verify         # rerun the analysis; fails unless every paper number is reproduced byte for byte (GATED=1)
make numbers paper  # regenerate every number and the PDF (GATED=1)
```

Requirements: [uv](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), and [tectonic](https://tectonic-typesetting.github.io/) for the PDF.

GPU stages (activations, generation, scoring) ran on a Colab A100, driven by `scripts/colab_gen.sh`. It needs
`COLAB_SSH_KEY` and an HF token with access to the gated Tiny Aya repos; its header documents the arguments and the
token handling. Comparisons never mix hardware: every steering arm is paired with an unrepaired reference generated
on the same A100 (`E0_a100`).

| Repository | Access | Contents |
|---|---|---|
| [`refusal-parity`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity) | open | Prompts, per-response labels (no response text), every summary file, paper and figures |
| [`refusal-parity-responses`](https://huggingface.co/datasets/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity-responses) | gated | Model responses (some harmful), judge-validation items |
| [`refusal-parity-steering`](https://huggingface.co/abdullahabtahi/refusal-parity-steering) | gated | Steering vectors, condition directions, thresholds, activations |

## Repository layout

```
src/        the refusal_parity package: one subpackage per pipeline stage (table above)
scripts/    remote-GPU drivers, release build, data fetch, reproduction check
tests/      unit tests: statistics, gate routing, label loading, data invariants
paper/      LaTeX sources, generated numbers and tables, figures with provenance JSON, PDF
docs/       README visuals and HTML/SVG sources (banner, pipeline diagram, dark-theme data charts)
research/   pre-registration and deviations log, premortems, research diary
release/    Hugging Face card templates (filled from the paper's numbers) and licence texts
```

**Determinism.**
- Seeds are fixed: data splits and the per-language paired bootstrap {{seed}}; tier and difference-in-differences bootstraps {{boot_seed}}; calibration fold split {{split_seed}}.
- Decoding is greedy.
- A100 and Apple-MPS generations differ slightly, so results are reported per hardware (`runs/E0_a100/hardware_check.json`).

## Pre-registration and research record

- [`research/00_research_plan.md`](research/00_research_plan.md): the analysis plan and its dated deviations log. Every
  design change is logged before the result it concerns.
- [`research/11_controls_premortem.md`](research/11_controls_premortem.md): the controls added after independent review.
- [`research/DIARY.md`](research/DIARY.md): decisions, failures and lessons, in order.

## AI use

Implementation and drafting were a collaboration between the author and an AI agent (Claude, Anthropic, via
Claude Code). Independent AI reviewer agents critiqued drafts and code, and every number is generated from the
result files by script. The paper's AI-use disclosure gives details.
